learning: If s-bend and oval progress both rise with max_error near or below 0.06 m, refine the lead between 0.04 and 0.05 m. If oscillation rises sharply or line-loss events increase, the lead optimum is near 0.03 m, and the next lever is wheel_track (0.09 to 0.10 m) or mass.
notes: Single-variable test of sensor lead: iteration-1 package with the sensor row moved from y 0.03 m to y 0.04 m. Controller is identical to iteration 1, so the lead is the only change.
rationale: Iteration 1 (sensor lead 0.03 m, 5 sensors at 0.025 m spacing, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.035, mass 0.6, body 0.14 x 0.10, kp 2.5, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.5) is the best measured design at 114.4. Every run in every iteration ended off track with zero finishes. Max error sits at 0.061 to 0.068 m, just above the 0.06 m floor, while RMS error stays at 0.023 to 0.031 m, so the robot tracks well until a single bend excursion. The lead is the one geometry variable I have only partly isolated. Iteration 5 moved it to 0.02 m, with everything else as in iteration 1, and the result was worse: score 91.8, s-bend progress 0.11 (against 0.26), oval progress 0.44 (against 0.47), and oscillation down to 0.24. That points to look-ahead being valuable on bends, so I test the other side of the lead at 0.04 m. The geometry follows entity0 exactly: the iteration-1 layout with the sensor row at y = 0.04 m. The controller is iteration 1 unchanged, including the same kp, kd, base_speed and sensor weights. Holding the controller fixed keeps the lead as the only variable, so any change in progress, max_error or oscillation can be attributed to it. Expected result (not measured): s-bend progress above 0.26, oval progress at or above 0.47, and max_error at or below about 0.06 m. Risk: the longer look-ahead may lag on the tightest bends, raising oscillation and line-loss events on the slalom.
